messages.content:
You are an expert requirements engineer evaluating User Stories using the Quality User Story (QUS) framework by Lucassen et al.

Your task is classification, not rewriting. Judge ONLY the QUS criterion supplied in the task. Do not invent additional defect categories. Do not penalize stylistic preferences unless they are directly relevant to the supplied criterion.

Use the entire project backlog only when the supplied criterion requires set-level comparison or when contextual interpretation is explicitly necessary. When the criterion is story-level, assess each target story primarily from its own text.

For every target story, return exactly one binary decision:
- "Violation": the story violates the supplied QUS criterion.
- "No Violation": the story does not violate the supplied QUS criterion.

Also return concise evidence and rationale. For set-level criteria, list related story IDs when the decision depends on another story. Do not use "Uncertain" or "Insufficient Context" in model outputs: the Gold Standard may contain such labels, but these are excluded from the primary binary effectiveness metrics.

Return valid JSON only, with this shape:
{
  "evaluations": [
    {
      "story_id": "...",
      "criterion": "...",
      "decision": "Violation|No Violation",
      "evidence": "short text span or empty string",
      "rationale": "short criterion-specific justification",
      "related_story_ids": [],
      "confidence": "High|Moderate|Low"
    }
  ]
}

Every target story ID must appear exactly once. Do not add prose outside the JSON object.

QUS CRITERION
Name: Full sentence
Dimension: Pragmatic
Scope: individual
Definition: A user story is a well-formed full sentence.
Operational decision rule: Violation when the text is a fragment, grammatically incomplete, or malformed enough that it does not read as a complete sentence. Minor typos that do not break sentence completeness should not automatically be defects.
Lucassen-derived example: A fragment such as 'Server configuration' is not a complete user-story sentence.

PROJECT
PlanningPoker

FULL BACKLOG
PP-001: As a moderator, I want to create a new game by entering a name and an optional description, so that I can start inviting estimators.
PP-002: As a moderator, I want to invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game, so that we can start the game.
PP-003: As a moderator, I want to start a round by entering an item in a single multi-line text field, so that we can estimate it.
PP-004: As a moderator, I want to see all items we try to estimate this session, so that I can answer questions about the current story such as "does this include ___".
PP-005: As a moderator, I want to select an item to be estimated or re-estimated, so that the team sees that item and can estimate it.
PP-006: As a moderator, I want to add an item to the list of items to be estimated, so that so that we can be flexible and accommodate situations where we think of a new story while playing.
PP-007: As a moderator, I want to edit an item in the list of items to be estimated, so that I can make it better reflect the team's understanding of the item.
PP-008: As a moderator, I want to delete an item from the list of items to be estimated, so that we can remove it and not estimate it.
PP-009: As a moderator, I want to show all estimates immediately, so that I can decide to show the estimates that have been given even though not all estimators have given their estimate.
PP-010: As a moderator, I want to accept the average of all estimates, so that we can move on to the next item when we agree.
PP-011: As a moderator, I want to have the "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card, so that I can accept it more quickly.
PP-012: As a moderator, I want to enter the agreed-upon estimate, so that we can move on to the next item when we agree.
PP-013: As a moderator, I want to estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again, so that we can give a new estimate if we feel different about the story after estimating other related stories.
PP-014: As a moderator, I want to import stories from a spreadsheet, so that I don't have to copy and paste each individual story.
PP-015: As a moderator, I want to copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet, so that I can get started more quickly.
PP-016: As a moderator, I want to browse through previous games, so that I can find the previous game I'm looking for.
PP-017: As a moderator, I want to view a transcript of a game, so that I can see the stories and estimates.
PP-018: As a moderator, I want to export a transcript of a game as a HTML file, so that I can save the stories and estimates locally.
PP-019: As a moderator, I want to export a transcript of a game as a CSV file, so that I can further process the stories and estimates.
PP-020: As a moderator, I want to delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored.
PP-021: As a moderator, I want to create an account for the application by entering my name, email address, a password and a username, so that I can start using the application.
PP-022: As a moderator, I want to log in using my account name and password, so that I can start using the application.
PP-023: As a moderator, I want to change my account details, so that I can keep my account details up-to-date.
PP-024: As a moderator, I want to delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored.
PP-025: As a moderator, I want to see dates and times in my local timezone, so that I don't have to do timezone conversion myself.
PP-026: As a moderator, I want to get a password reminder by email, so that I can get back to using the application when I've forgotten my password.
PP-027: As a moderator, I want to select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}, so that the team can use either the modified Fibonacci sequence or powers of 2.
PP-028: As a moderator, I want to invite up to 15 estimators, so that we can play with large but not immense teams.
PP-029: As an estimator, I want to join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for, so that I can participate.
PP-030: As an estimator, I want to see the item we're estimating, so that I know what I'm giving an estimate for.
PP-031: As an estimator, I want to see all items we will try to estimate this session, so that I have a feel for the sizes of the various items.
PP-032: As a participant, I want to immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator, so that I know who has already given an estimate and who we're still waiting for.
PP-033: As a participant, I want to be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate, so that I can be sure estimates are independent and not influenced by other estimates given in the same draw.
PP-034: As a participant, I want to be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown, so that I can change my mind based on information I hear.
PP-035: As a participant, I want to be able to see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated, so that I can see how his or her opinion has changed so I can ask questions.
PP-036: As a participant, I want to see who gave what estimates during the current round, so that I know this when we're discussing the estimates.
PP-037: As a participant, I want to be able start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see, so that I can limit the time spent discussing the estimates when I think we've talked long enough.
PP-038: As a participant, I want to have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate, so that it's ready for use on the next round.
PP-039: As a participant, I want to scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds, so that I can use this information when I estimate the item of the current round.
PP-040: As a participant, I want to always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws, so that it's easy to compare estimates.
PP-041: As a participant, I want to change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed, so that I can change my mind.
PP-042: As a participant, I want to have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played, so that the game is more personal because I see who I'm estimating with.
PP-043: As a developer, I want to have written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards, so that as many people as possible can access the site and view it as intended.
PP-044: As a developer, I want to have a list of definitions for commonly used terms, so that everyone working on the project can understand each other more easily.
PP-045: As a developer, I want to have created database indexes, so that the queries run as fast as possible.
PP-046: As a developer, I want to have the application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2, so that as many people as possible can fully use the application.
PP-047: As a developer, I want to have the site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible, so that people with accessibility issues can use the application.
PP-048: As a user, I want to have the application respond quickly to my actions, so that I don't get bored.
PP-049: As a user, I want to be able to use Unicode, so that I can use any language I like.
PP-050: As a user, I want to see sensible and predictable URLs, so that the application feels logical and transparent.
PP-051: As a user, I want to have nice error pages when something goes wrong, so that I can trust the system and its developers.
PP-052: As a Researcher, I want results to be stored in a non-identifiable way, so that I can study the data to see things like whether estimates converged around the first opinion given by "estimator A" for example.
PP-053: As a Mike, I want to be able to see some metrics on use of the game, so that I can see how much it is being used.

TASK
Evaluate EVERY story in the backlog for the single criterion "Full sentence".
Do not evaluate any other QUS criterion in this call.
If the criterion is set-level, compare stories across the full backlog and identify related story IDs when relevant.
If the criterion is individual-level, do not treat a problem belonging solely to another QUS criterion as evidence for this criterion.
Return exactly 53 evaluation objects, one for each story ID.
